title: Passover Instructions
english: The precious blood of Christ stops the wrath of God, delivering those who are sanctified from corruption, because life comes from life, and God is the source of all life, just as God is from God.
According to Scripture, the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron in the land of Egypt, saying, 'This month is the beginning of months, it is the first for you' (Exodus 12:2).
The Lord instructed Moses to speak to the whole assembly of the sons of Israel, telling them to take a lamb according to the houses of the fathers, a lamb according to a house.

If there are few in the house, they shall take with them their nearest neighbor. Then they shall take a designated lamb, and it shall be perfect, without blemish, a year old, taken from the sheep or the goats, and it shall be kept for you until the fourteenth of the month.
The whole assembly of the sons of Israel was to slaughter the lamb in the evening, and take some of the blood and put it on the two doorposts and on the lintel of the houses.

They were to eat the flesh in the night, roasted by fire, with unleavened bread and bitter herbs, as the Lord commanded, 'You shall not eat any of it raw or boiled in water, but roasted by fire, with its head and feet and entrails' (Exodus 12:9).
They were not to leave any of it until morning, and they were not to break any of its bones, and what was left of it until morning was to be burned with fire.

The lawgiver adds to these things, teaching what kind of figure the feasters should be and in what manner those who have been perfected should touch the common sacred things. He again determines what kind of sacrifice is appropriate, and how it is to be performed.

For he says: 'Thus you will eat it; your loins will be girded, and your sandals will be on your feet, and your staffs will be in your hands; and you will eat it with haste' (Exodus 12:11). For it is the Passover of the Lord.

The Lord says, 'I will pass through the land of Egypt, and I will strike every firstborn from man to beast, and I will execute vengeance on all the gods of the Egyptians; I am the Lord' (Exodus 12:12).

The blood of the lamb will serve as a sign for the people, protecting them from the plague that will destroy the Egyptians, as the Lord says, 'And the blood will be a sign for you on the houses where you are, and I will see the blood, and I will protect you, and there will not be a plague among you to destroy when I strike the land of Egypt' (Exodus 12:13).

The people are also instructed to eat unleavened bread for seven days, removing leaven from their houses on the first day, as the Lord commands, 'For seven days you will eat unleavened bread, and from the first day, you will remove leaven from your houses' (Exodus 12:15).
And having determined the punishment for the one who transgresses, he says again: And the day…

title: Baptismal Conformity to Christ
english: Through holy baptism, we die with Christ and are conformed to him, so that we may also share in his resurrection. This is the teaching of Paul, who writes that we were buried with Christ through baptism into death, and just as Christ was raised from the dead through the glory of the Father, we too may walk in newness of life (Romans 6:4). As we are conformed to the knowledge of truth through faith, and have already been enriched with conformity to our Lord Jesus Christ, who is the firstborn for us and in us, we drink the pure milk of the word, advancing to the measure of the fullness of Christ.

Then, as the scripture says, we will all be holy and a sacrifice to God, dying to the world but living to God in a holy manner. For you have died, and your life is hidden with Christ in God (Colossians 3:3). This is the death that is precious in the sight of the Lord, as the psalmist says. It is a death that is holy, and one that we experience notionally, through our faith and our baptism.

The lamb was being nourished, namely the calf for seven days by its mother; then it was being brought near according to the eighth, enigmatically, I think, with God revealing (for the law is a shadow), as it was necessary to be instructed beforehand through types and lessons, like children, in order to become the future holy ones and to be brought to the scent of fragrance to God.

The time most suitable for such completion is the mystery of Christ, which is signified through the eighth. God is inaccessible through legal worship, but through Christ alone, we can approach Him. The law has accomplished nothing, but Christ brings it to this point, making those who have believed perfect in virtue and giving them the perfect thing in knowledge through Himself. We have the same mind as Christ, and through Him and with Him and the Holy Spirit, glory to God and the Father for ages of ages.

title: Rejection of Divine Guidance
english: The Jews were rejecting the use of earthly things according to the world, and necessarily they were stumbling, not only against the one God of all, but also against the divine Moses, for they had been given shadows of the things to come, and types of the later events that had already occurred.

Having been settled for us from above and from heaven, the truest manna, Christ, who is able to nourish and promising an unbounded life, they were foolishly and excessively rejecting, and it is written that the Lord was angry with his people, and it was evil before Moses (Numbers 11:1).

One could learn from the evangelical parable that the crowd of Jews was setting before them the fleeting and fleshly goods from above, rather than the true and nourishing manna, Christ, for the dinner invitees wanted to gather for the weddings, but they were going away, one to his own field, the other to his business, making excuses for not attending, such as one saying he had married a wife, and the other saying he had bought a field and could not come.

The mind of the saints always follows the votes of God, and it is always the case that the mind of the saints follows God's judgments, and Moses himself was crying out against the disobedience of the Jews, as our Lord Jesus Christ says: Do not think that I will accuse you before the Father, for there is one who accuses you, Moses, in whom you have hoped (John 5:45).

If you believe Moses, you would believe me, for he wrote about me, and Moses considers it a burden to bear the Israelites anymore, but God was sanctifying others, seventy in number, as we have already said, to lead, and the law alone, of which Moses is a type, is not able to lead us.

The number seventy holds significant meaning, as these individuals, along with others, were ordained to fulfill the remaining needs, thereby completing the number and making it perfect, and they were brought near to Moses through Christ to lead, and the apostles, as the firstfruits and fathers, were among them.

God is said to have taken away from the spirit that was on Moses and given it to the chosen ones, so that we may believe that the one and holy Spirit sanctifies both the saints who came before us and us, and this is evident because the Father is one, the Son is one, and the Holy Spirit is also one, present in both the prophets and in us, and although it is undivided, it is fully present in all, with the distribution of many gifts.
We must observe that God, who is over all, commanded the chosen seventy to be gathered, but they are not complete, for two, Modad and Eldad, are missing, and those who are lacking are also rebuked…
